# Welcome (/docs/)

ProofPay holds community donations in escrow on PayPal and releases each stage payment only when photo evidence passes deterministic checks plus two independent AI reviewers. Plain code makes the decision. A human verifier handles held cases, and every step goes into a hash-chained audit log.

This portal, the SDKs and the agent plugin are all generated from one OpenAPI spec, [`openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/shreesh1802/tollgate/blob/main/openapi.yaml), which a test keeps in sync with the real server.

## How a payment moves [#how-a-payment-moves]

1. **Reserve.** A donor creates a donation. PayPal authorizes it (`intent: AUTHORIZE`), so the money stays in their account.
2. **Prove.** The worker uploads a photo for the active stage with that stage's one-time code in it.
3. **Decide.** The gate checks for duplicates, location, time and the code, and asks two AI reviewers. It returns `RELEASE`, `RESUBMIT`, `HOLD` or `BLOCK`.
4. **Release.** On `RELEASE` each donor's exact share is captured and the worker is paid. On `HOLD` a human verifier decides.

## Who can call what [#who-can-call-what]

| Role | Header | Can do |
|---|---|---|
| Anyone | none | read projects and the audit log, donate |
| Worker | `X-Worker-Key` | upload evidence, see the active stage's code |
| Verifier | `X-Verifier-Key` | read the queue, approve or reject |

## Try it [#try-it]

The live demo runs simulated payments with real AI reviewers: [proofpay-on99.onrender.com](https://proofpay-on99.onrender.com).

# Context Plugin (/docs/context-plugin)

The context plugin teaches your AI coding assistant how to use this API's SDKs, so the code it writes for you calls the API the way the SDKs are meant to be used.

## Install [#install]

```bash
npx context-plugins install "https://proofpay-on99.onrender.com/docs/__downloads/plugin.zip"
```

## What it does [#what-it-does]

Once the plugin is installed, describe what you want to build and your assistant works from the SDK for your language: how to install it and create a client, how to authenticate, and which methods and types to use for each call. You spend less time correcting code written from guesses about the API.

## Supported languages [#supported-languages]

- TypeScript
- Python

## Supported platforms [#supported-platforms]

- Claude Code
- Cursor
- GitHub Copilot

# Python SDK (/docs/sdks/python)

[Download SDK](/docs/__downloads/sdk/python.zip)

## Intro [#intro]

The ProofPay API SDK provides access to the [ProofPay API REST APIs](https://github.com/shreesh1802/tollgate).

ProofPay holds community donations in escrow on PayPal and releases each stage payment
only when photo evidence passes deterministic checks plus two independent AI reviewers.
Plain code makes the decision; a human verifier handles held cases; every step is written
to a hash-chained audit log.

**Who can call what**

| Role | How it identifies itself | Can do |
|---|---|---|
| Anyone | nothing | read projects and the audit log, donate |
| Worker | `X-Worker-Key` (returned when the project is created) | upload evidence, see the current one-time code |
| Verifier | `X-Verifier-Key` | read the review queue, approve or reject |
| Organiser | `X-Organizer-Key` (only if the server sets one) | create projects |

Money amounts are decimal strings or numbers in the project's currency (USD). The payee's
email address is never returned by any endpoint.

## Installation [#installation]

Add the SDK to your project from its folder, with whichever package manager your project uses. Give each tool a path containing a slash, such as `../proof-pay-api` — a bare folder name is looked up on PyPI instead, and resolves to whatever project holds that name there:

```bash
pip install <path-to-sdk>
```

```bash
uv add <path-to-sdk>
```

```bash
poetry add <path-to-sdk>
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

### Synchronous client [#synchronous-client]

Construct `ProofPayApiClient` with keyword arguments, and call `close()` when you are done. Every argument is optional.

```python
from proof_pay_api import ProofPayApiClient

client = ProofPayApiClient(
    worker_key="YOUR_API_KEY", verifier_key="YOUR_API_KEY", organizer_key="YOUR_API_KEY", environment="production"
)

client.close()
```

Alternatively, scope it — `with ProofPayApiClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

### Asynchronous client [#asynchronous-client]

`AsyncProofPayApiClient` mirrors `ProofPayApiClient` with **identical method names**, and every endpoint method is a coroutine. It takes the same arguments, with some differences — for example, the transport argument is `custom_async_http_client`.

```python
from asyncio import run

from proof_pay_api import AsyncProofPayApiClient

async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncProofPayApiClient(
        worker_key="YOUR_API_KEY", verifier_key="YOUR_API_KEY", organizer_key="YOUR_API_KEY", environment="production"
    )
    await client.aclose()

run(main())
```

Alternatively, scope it — `async with AsyncProofPayApiClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

# TypeScript SDK (/docs/sdks/typescript)

[Download SDK](/docs/__downloads/sdk/typescript.zip)

## Intro [#intro]

The ProofPay API SDK provides access to the [ProofPay API REST APIs](https://github.com/shreesh1802/tollgate).

ProofPay holds community donations in escrow on PayPal and releases each stage payment
only when photo evidence passes deterministic checks plus two independent AI reviewers.
Plain code makes the decision; a human verifier handles held cases; every step is written
to a hash-chained audit log.

**Who can call what**

| Role | How it identifies itself | Can do |
|---|---|---|
| Anyone | nothing | read projects and the audit log, donate |
| Worker | `X-Worker-Key` (returned when the project is created) | upload evidence, see the current one-time code |
| Verifier | `X-Verifier-Key` | read the review queue, approve or reject |
| Organiser | `X-Organizer-Key` (only if the server sets one) | create projects |

Money amounts are decimal strings or numbers in the project's currency (USD). The payee's
email address is never returned by any endpoint.

## Installation [#installation]

The SDK compiles to `dist/` before it can be referenced — run its `build` script once in the SDK folder, then add it to your project by path:

```bash
npm install <path-to-sdk>
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

Create one client and reuse it. Configure its behaviour through `ClientOptions`.

```ts
import { ProofPayApiClient, ServerEnvironment } from "proof-pay-api";

const client = new ProofPayApiClient({
  serverEnvironment: ServerEnvironment.Production,
  workerKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
  verifierKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
  organizerKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
});
```

Nothing in `ClientOptions` is required — `new ProofPayApiClient()` compiles — and each option left out falls back to its default. `serverEnvironment` is spelled out above so the environment a call reaches is visible where the client is built rather than inherited silently.

### From CommonJS [#from-commonjs]

The package ships both dialects from a single entry, so `require` works with full types. In a TypeScript CommonJS file use the `import ... = require(...)` form — a plain destructuring `require` runs fine but gives you `any`.

```ts
import sdk = require("proof-pay-api");

const client = new sdk.ProofPayApiClient({
  serverEnvironment: sdk.ServerEnvironment.Production,
  workerKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
  verifierKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
  organizerKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
});
```

# Liveness check (/docs/api/openapi/service/getHealth)

`GET /api/health`

`uptimeSeconds` lets an operator tell a restarting process from a routing problem.

# How this server is configured (/docs/api/openapi/service/getConfig)

`GET /api/config`

Tells a client whether payments are mock or sandbox, whether reviews are simulated, and the upload size limit.

# List projects (/docs/api/openapi/projects/listProjects)

`GET /api/projects`

Also refreshes any payouts that PayPal has accepted but not yet settled.

# Create a project (/docs/api/openapi/projects/createProject)

`POST /api/projects`

Stage percentages must add up to 100. Each stage has a time window in which its evidence
must be photographed. The response contains the worker key; keep it, it is shown once.


# Read one project (/docs/api/openapi/projects/getProject)

`GET /api/projects/{id}`

The public view: donations, totals, stages and each stage's submissions. Send
`X-Worker-Key` to also receive the one-time code of the active stage.


# Read the audit log and check its hash chain (/docs/api/openapi/projects/getAuditLog)

`GET /api/projects/{id}/audit`

Every decision is an entry that includes the hash of the one before it, so altering history breaks the chain.

# Reserve a donation on PayPal (/docs/api/openapi/donations/createDonation)

`POST /api/projects/{id}/donations`

Creates a PayPal order with intent AUTHORIZE: the money stays in the donor's account and
is only reserved. On the sandbox, send the donor to `approveUrl` to approve it; they are
then returned to the site and the reservation is confirmed. In mock mode there is no
approval step and the donation is confirmed immediately.


# PayPal return link (browser redirect) (/docs/api/openapi/donations/donationReturn)

`GET /api/donate/return`

PayPal sends the donor's browser here after approval with `?token=<order id>`. It confirms
the reservation and redirects back to the site. This is not meant to be called by an API client.


# Upload photo evidence for a stage (/docs/api/openapi/evidence/submitEvidence)

`POST /api/projects/{id}/stages/{stageId}/submissions`

The body is the raw image (JPEG or PNG), not a form. The server checks for duplicates,
location and time from the photo's metadata, and that the one-time code is visible, then
asks two independent AI reviewers. The deterministic gate decides: RELEASE, RESUBMIT,
HOLD (a human decides) or BLOCK. On RELEASE each donor's share is captured and the worker
is paid.

On a demo server with simulated reviewers, `demoCode`, `demoMatch` and `demoFlags` steer
the simulated reviewers; they are ignored when real reviewers are used.


# Fetch an evidence photo (/docs/api/openapi/evidence/getEvidenceImage)

`GET /api/images/{projectId}/{subId}`

Public only after the submission has released funds. Before that, the worker or verifier key is required.

# Submissions waiting for a human (/docs/api/openapi/verification/getVerifierQueue)

`GET /api/verify/queue`

Submissions the gate held for review, and ones whose payment release failed and needs a retry.

# Approve or reject a held submission (/docs/api/openapi/verification/decideSubmission)

`POST /api/verify/{projectId}/{submissionId}`

Approval is bound to the evidence the verifier saw: send the `evidenceHash` from the queue
item. If the evidence changed since, the call fails with 409 and nothing is released.
